segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: At that time Jesus went through the grainfields on the Sabbath. His disciples were hungry, and they began to pluck heads of grain and eat.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: But the Pharisees saw it and said to him,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “Look, your disciples are doing what is not permitted on a Sabbath.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: He said to them,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “Have you not read what David did when he was hungry, he and those with him:

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: how he entered the house of God, and they ate the loaves of presentation, which it was not permitted for him to eat, nor for those with him, but only for the priests?

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: Or have you not read in the Law that on the Sabbath the priests in the temple profane the Sabbath and are guiltless?

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: I tell you that something greater than the temple is here.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: If you had known what this means, ‘I desire mercy and not sacrifice,’ you would not have condemned the guiltless.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: For the Son of Man is lord of the Sabbath.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Moving on from there, he went into their synagogue.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: And there was a man with a withered hand. They questioned him, asking,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “Is it permitted to heal on the Sabbath?”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: They asked this so that they might bring a charge against him.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: He said to them,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “Which of you, having a single sheep, if it falls into a pit on the Sabbath, will not take hold of it and lift it out?

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: How much more valuable, then, is a person than a sheep! So it is permitted to do good on the Sabbath.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Then he said to the man,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “Stretch out your hand.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: He stretched it out, and it was restored, as sound as the other.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: But the Pharisees went out and plotted against him, how they might destroy him.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Jesus, aware of this, withdrew from there. Many followed him, and he healed them all,

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: and he sternly ordered them not to make him known,

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: so that what was spoken through Isaiah the prophet might be fulfilled:

segments.speaker: scripture
segments.text: “Look, my servant whom I have chosen, my beloved, in whom my soul delights. I will put my Spirit upon him, and he will announce justice to the Gentiles.

segments.speaker: scripture
segments.text: He will not quarrel or cry out, nor will anyone hear his voice in the streets.

segments.speaker: scripture
segments.text: A bruised reed he will not break, and a smoldering wick he will not put out, until he brings justice through to victory.

segments.speaker: scripture
segments.text: And in his name the Gentiles will hope.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Then a demon-possessed man who was blind and mute was brought to him, and he healed him, so that the mute man could speak and see.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: All the crowds were amazed and said,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “Could this be the Son of David?”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: But when the Pharisees heard it, they said,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “This man does not drive out demons except by Beelzebul, the ruler of the demons.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Knowing their thoughts, he said to them,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “Every kingdom divided against itself is laid waste, and no city or household divided against itself will stand.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: And if Satan drives out Satan, he is divided against himself; how then will his kingdom stand?

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: And if I drive out demons by Beelzebul, by whom do your sons drive them out? For this reason they themselves will be your judges.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: But if it is by the Spirit of God that I drive out demons, then the kingdom of God has come upon you.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: Or how can anyone enter the strong man’s house and seize his goods unless he first ties up the strong man? Then he will plunder his house.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: Whoever is not with me is against me, and whoever does not gather with me scatters.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: For this reason I tell you, people will be forgiven every sin and blasphemy, but the blasphemy against the Spirit will not be forgiven.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: And whoever speaks a word against the Son of Man will be forgiven, but whoever speaks against the Holy Spirit will not be forgiven, either in this age or in the one to come.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: Either make the tree good and its fruit good, or make the tree rotten and its fruit rotten; for the tree is known by its fruit.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: Brood of vipers! How can you speak good things when you are evil? For out of the overflow of the heart the mouth speaks.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: The good person brings good things out of a good store, and the evil person brings evil things out of an evil store.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: But I tell you that for every idle word people speak, they will give an account on the day of judgment;

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: for by your words you will be vindicated, and by your words you will be condemned.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Then some of the scribes and Pharisees responded to him,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “Teacher, we want to see a sign from you.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: But he answered them,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “An evil and adulterous generation seeks a sign, and no sign will be given to it except the sign of Jonah the prophet.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: For just as Jonah was in the belly of the sea monster three days and three nights, so the Son of Man will be in the heart of the earth three days and three nights.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: The men of Nineveh will rise up at the judgment with this generation and condemn it, because they turned back at Jonah’s proclamation, and look, something more than Jonah is here.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: The queen of the South will be raised at the judgment with this generation and condemn it, because she came from the ends of the earth to hear the wisdom of Solomon, and look, something more than Solomon is here.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: When the unclean spirit comes out of a person, it passes through waterless places seeking rest, and does not find it.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: Then it says, ‘I will return to my house, from which I came out.’ And when it comes, it finds the house unoccupied, swept, and put in order.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: Then it goes and brings along with it seven other spirits more evil than itself, and they go in and settle there; and that person’s last state becomes worse than the first. So it will be also with this evil generation.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: While he was still speaking to the crowds, there were his mother and his brothers, standing outside and seeking to speak to him.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Someone said to him,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “Look, your mother and your brothers are standing outside, seeking to speak to you.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: But he replied to the one who told him,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “Who is my mother, and who are my brothers?”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: And stretching out his hand toward his disciples, he said,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “Look, my mother and my brothers!

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: For whoever does the will of my Father in the heavens, that one is my brother and sister and mother.”

notes.traditional: the showbread / the bread of the Presence
notes.note: These are the twelve loaves set out each Sabbath on a table in the sanctuary and afterwards eaten only by priests (Leviticus 24:5–9); the David story is in 1 Samuel 21. The Greek phrase means 'the loaves of the setting-out'. 'Bread of the Presence', used by most modern translations, renders the Hebrew expression behind it rather than the Greek.

The Greek adjective is neuter, 'something greater', not masculine, 'someone greater'; some later manuscripts have the masculine, which lies behind older English versions. Most interpreters take the neuter as an indirect reference to Jesus himself or to the kingdom arriving in his work. The same neuter construction recurs in verses 41 and 42 with a different word, rendered 'something more'.

The quotation is Isaiah 42:1–4, in a form that differs from the standard Greek version and is at points closer to the Hebrew. The Greek word can mean either 'servant' or 'child'; the Hebrew behind it means 'servant', and that is the usual rendering. The wording 'my beloved, in whom my soul delights' echoes the voice at Jesus's baptism (3:17).

The same Greek word is translated 'judgment' in verses 36, 41 and 42. Here and in verse 20 it stands for the Hebrew term in Isaiah that means right order or just rule, so most modern translations have 'justice'. Older versions have 'judgment', and some interpreters think Matthew does intend the announcement of a coming verdict.

Greek has one word for 'nations' and 'Gentiles'; in the plural it regularly means the non-Jewish peoples. 'The nations' would be an equally possible rendering here and in verse 21. Matthew's point is that Isaiah foresaw the servant's work reaching beyond Israel.

A name for the ruler of the demons, whom verse 26 equates with Satan. Its origin is disputed. It may be connected with Baal-zebub, the god of Ekron in 2 Kings 1, and the spelling 'Beelzebub' in older English Bibles comes by way of the Latin tradition, not from the Greek manuscripts.

'Sons' is a Semitic way of speaking of the members of a group, here probably exorcists belonging to the Pharisees' own circle, and need not mean their literal children. Jewish exorcism was a known practice in the period. The argument is that the charge against Jesus would condemn their own people as well.

Greek has one word-family where English has two (righteous and just, righteousness and justice, justify). The verb here is courtroom language: to be declared in the right at the judgment, the opposite of 'condemned'. Most translations have 'justified' or 'acquitted'.

The word is used in the prophets' figurative sense, as in Hosea and Ezekiel, where Israel's unfaithfulness to God is pictured as a wife's unfaithfulness to her husband. It is not an accusation about sexual conduct.

The Greek word means any huge sea creature and does not name a particular species. It is the word the Greek version of Jonah uses for the Hebrew 'great fish'. 'Whale' in older English Bibles is more specific than the Greek, and 'great fish' in many modern ones follows the Hebrew of Jonah instead of Matthew's word.

'Repent' now suggests mainly feeling sorry. The Greek word carries the prophets' call to return to God, a change of direction in mind and conduct, which is what the people of Nineveh do in Jonah 3. Most translations keep 'repented' as an established term understood to include a change of life.

Some early and important manuscripts lack this verse. It may have been dropped by accident, since it ends with the same Greek words as verse 46 and a copyist's eye could skip from one to the other. Verse 48 also presupposes that someone has spoken, so this edition prints the verse, though some editions bracket it as doubtful.
The Greek is plural, a Semitic turn of phrase characteristic of Matthew that a first-century hearer would have noticed. Most translations flatten it to 'heaven'.

candidates.reason: The word covers the act of judging, the verdict and justice as right order, and translators split differently in the Isaiah citations and in John, so the dividing line should be fixed once.
It recurs throughout the Sabbath and divorce controversies and in Paul, and English varies between 'lawful', 'permitted' and 'allowed' in ways that hide the repeated term.
In period usage it means abusive or slanderous speech against people as well as against God, so the choice between 'blasphemy' and 'slander' needs one policy across the Gospels, Paul and Revelation.
Translations vary between 'age', 'world' and 'eternity'/'forever' in its idioms, and this affects many theologically loaded passages.
'Possessed' imports a model the Greek verb does not specify, and the rendering (demon-possessed, demonized, afflicted by a demon) should be consistent across the Gospels.
